re_line: APEC Shenzhen: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral looms · Quad unveils defence and minerals deals · Canberra sanctions Israeli settler leader · US pledges $450m to Palau, FSM, Marshalls · Fiji declares drought disaster
morning_memo: Washington committed more than $450 million in new Compact of Free Association funding to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia and the Marshall Islands for the 2027 financial year, under agreements granting the United States exclusive defence rights in all three.

Quad leaders meeting in Manila announced new defence and critical-minerals cooperation, with Donald Trump calling the grouping 'very important' before Anthony Albanese flew on to Shenzhen for Thursday's unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral at APEC.

Fiji declared a state of national disaster over El Nino drought, giving Suva powers of mandatory evacuation, curfew and water rationing, while category 5 Cyclone Xavier bore down on the Northern Cook Islands with gusts to 315km/h.

top_stories.headline: US adds $450 million to Palau, FSM and Marshall Islands compact funding
top_stories.body: The United States will provide more than *$450 million* in new funding to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia and the Marshall Islands for the 2027 financial year under updated Compact of Free Association agreements. Palau receives over $41 million, the FSM $140 million, and the Marshall Islands more than $171 million, plus a final $100 million contribution to its Compact Trust Fund. The agreements grant Washington exclusive defence rights in the three states, part of a 20-year, $7.1 billion package. The funding follows annual meetings in September between US officials and the three governments.
top_stories.src_line: per RNZ Pacific: "Palau, FSM and Marshall Islands to recieve $450 million funding boost from US"

top_stories.headline: Quad leaders announce defence and critical-minerals deals in Manila
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** sat down with **Donald Trump**, Japan's Sanae Takaichi and India's **Narendra Modi** for the first Quad leaders' meeting Trump has attended in person. The group announced new joint military ventures after discussions on artificial intelligence and critical minerals, with Trump calling the grouping 'very important' and telling the leaders 'my phone is always open.' Trump said the minerals deals 'guarantee safety.' Albanese then flew to Shenzhen for APEC.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Quad leader unveil new defence and economic deals" · also SMH (Natassia Chrysanthos)

top_stories.headline: Australia sanctions Israeli settler leader Daniella Weiss
top_stories.body: Australia sanctioned three individuals and an organisation tied to Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank, among them **Daniella Weiss**, described by the ABC as the godmother of the settler movement, and Nachala, the organisation she leads. A construction company was also listed. The measures ban Australian people and businesses from trading with or providing financial or other support to those named. Foreign Minister **Penny Wong** announced the listings.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH Federal Politics (Matthew Knott): "Australia sanctions Israeli settlers, construction company" · also Reuters

overnight_items.headline: Albanese says Ukraine's fate at Shenzhen talks 'not up to Australia'
overnight_items.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** called for an end to global conflicts ahead of talks between **Donald Trump**, **Xi Jinping** and **Vladimir Putin**, while insisting Ukraine must have a say in its own future. He urged the three leaders not to waste what he called a historic opportunity to deliver peace, after touching down in Shenzhen for the APEC summit.

overnight_items.headline: Xi opens APEC with a pitch for free trade as Putin blasts sanctions
overnight_items.body_text: **Xi Jinping** opened the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen by promoting free trade and declaring China willing to work with other countries to build regional prosperity. The Australian reported Xi and **Vladimir Putin** using the forum to criticise Western protectionism and sanctions. The Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral is scheduled for Thursday on the summit's sidelines.

overnight_items.headline: Bowen tells COP31 it is 'not too late to turn down the temperature'
overnight_items.body_text: Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen delivered Australia's address at the COP31 conference in Turkey, arguing it is not too late to limit warming. The speech followed a think tank warning that Australia is not moving fast enough to meet its own emissions targets. The Australian separately reported BloombergNEF projecting Australia reaches *64 percent* renewables by 2030, short of Labor's target.

overnight_items.headline: Rio Tinto commits funds to Panguna mine remediation in Bougainville
overnight_items.body_text: Rio Tinto will pay to address environmental damage and human rights harm caused by the long-closed Panguna mine in Bougainville. ABC Pacific put the commitment at *$371 million*; the New York Times reported the landmark deal at $250 million. The two figures could not be reconciled from today's reporting.

overnight_items.headline: Budget-crunched Australian public sector leans into AI efficiencies
overnight_items.body_text: Politico reports the Australian public service turning to artificial intelligence for efficiency gains as budget pressure tightens across agencies. The reporting lands a day after this brief carried figures showing Canberra's digital traineeship program hired 73 people against a target of 1,000.

aukus_watch.headline: ASPI warns Collins-class refurbishment is overrunning, hitting availability
aukus_watch.body_text: Australia's plan to extend the lives of its Collins-class submarines is 'quietly unravelling,' the ASPI Strategist argues, warning of a high risk of downward-spiralling operational availability while the navy awaits the arrival and build-up of a nuclear-powered fleet. The piece flags workforce constraints as a driver.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji declares national disaster over El Nino drought
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji's Cabinet declared a state of national disaster on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council, empowering mandatory evacuations, curfews, travel restrictions, water rationing and land use rules. Prime Minister **Sitiveni Rabuka** said the declaration strengthens how government mobilises resources and coordinates assistance. He faced public backlash earlier this month for brushing off the drought's severity.

pacific_wire.headline: Category 5 Cyclone Xavier bears down on Pukapuka and Nassau
pacific_wire.body_text: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier strengthened from category 1 on Saturday to category 5 by Wednesday morning, with maximum sustained winds of about 220km/h and gusts to *315km/h*, according to the Fiji Meteorological Service. Cook Islands Meteorological Service director Maara Vaiimene said it is moving west-southwest past Pukapuka and Nassau and away from Manihiki and Rakahanga. Shelters have been activated.

pacific_wire.headline: Court blocks US seabed lease auction off American Samoa
pacific_wire.body_text: A court blocked the US government's seabed lease auction in American Samoa. Despite the ruling, the Marine Minerals Administration has not cancelled the November 19 sale in California, which would be the first deep-sea mining lease sale in the United States.

pacific_wire.headline: Solomon Islands drafts national loss and damage policy
pacific_wire.body_text: Solomon Islands is developing a national policy on climate change loss and damage after taking part in the launch of a regional framework. The work follows Honiara's year in the Pacific Islands Forum chair under Prime Minister **Jeremiah Manele**.

pacific_wire.headline: Niue wins 2026 Earthshot Prize for ocean conservation
pacific_wire.body_text: Niue took the 2026 Earthshot prize for ocean conservation, PACNEWS reported, in a bulletin that also recorded Singapore pledging *US$500,000* to the Pacific Resilience Facility and Vanuatu arguing the International Court of Justice advisory opinion must guide COP31 outcomes. Samoa told the conference the defining challenge is implementation rather than ambition.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu and Vanuatu join global push to end fossil fuel subsidies
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu and Vanuatu signed on to a global campaign to end fossil fuel subsidies, PACNEWS reported from COP31. The same bulletin carried Australian minister Chris Bowen saying Pacific-backed fossil fuel transition language must survive the negotiation, and Fiji reminding delegates that holding 1.5 degrees is a legal obligation.

pacific_wire.headline: Pacific presses for climate finance reform at COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: Pacific Islands Forum representatives told COP31 that international climate finance systems must be reformed to become meaningful for Pacific communities. The Australian reported 'worry' among Pacific leaders as their pleas at the conference went unanswered.

pacific_wire.headline: Deaths of conjoined twins prompt calls to fix PNG referral pathways
pacific_wire.body_text: Conjoined twin girls born on New Britain died of heart complications as a medical team prepared to evacuate them from Nonga Base Hospital. Pilot Jurgen Ruh, whose MAMA Foundation learned of the sisters 10 days after their birth, said: 'The ball was rolling and the ball should have been rolling 10 days earlier.' Janet Sios, whose Port Moresby private hospital had offered free treatment, called the outcome sad.

pacific_wire.headline: Tongan cancer care still depends on a three-hour flight
pacific_wire.body_text: Writing for World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, a Pacific Island Times contributor argues Tongan women cannot wait until 2040 for elimination targets. The quality of care available to the author's cousin came down to a three-hour plane ride, and she chose New Zealand.

new_zealand.headline: Luxon lands in Shenzhen for 23 hours of APEC diplomacy
new_zealand.body_text: Caretaker Prime Minister **Christopher Luxon** and caretaker Trade Minister **Todd McClay** arrive in Shenzhen for just 23 hours on the ground. Luxon attends the leaders' plenary and is expected to lunch with the leaders of Australia, Canada and Singapore; McClay meets US Trade Representative **Jamieson Greer** on Thursday. APEC economies buy *75 percent* of New Zealand's exports.

new_zealand.headline: Peters 'deeply concerned' by findings Russia used chemical weapons
new_zealand.body_text: Foreign Minister **Winston Peters** said findings that Russian forces dropped a grenade containing CS gas into a Ukrainian trench line in September 2024 are 'illegal in international law' and add to longstanding concerns about Russia's compliance with the Chemical Weapons Convention. The investigation was conducted by Ukraine and supported by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand mayor says democracy has 'had its day' after China visit
new_zealand.body_text: A New Zealand mayor said democracy has 'had its day' following a visit to China, AFP reported. The remark lands as Luxon travels to Shenzhen and amid continued scrutiny of subnational engagement between New Zealand local government and Chinese counterparts.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Devpolicy traces constituency funds from Taipei to Beijing to Canberra
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Terence Wood follows the money from a Weather Coast village to Canberra's new treaty, arguing that constituency funds in Solomon Islands, Taiwanese, then Chinese, and now Australian, reward loyal voters and punish the rest. Wood is a Fellow at the Development Policy Centre researching political governance in western Melanesia.

canberra_politics.headline: One Nation unveils second phase of immigration policy
canberra_politics.body_text: One Nation released the second phase of its immigration policy, drastically cutting humanitarian visas and abolishing parent visas entirely, the ABC's Politics Now reported. Separately, Pauline Hanson questioned Labor's migration intake from countries carrying 'do not travel' advisories.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor moves closer to passing gas reservation scheme after WA carve-out
canberra_politics.body_text: Labor is closer to passing its gas reservation scheme after effectively carving Western Australia out of the plan, ABC Politics Now reported. Radio National Breakfast set out the Coalition's four concerns with the proposal, a day after gas producers warned of 'dire consequences' over a WA carve-out.

canberra_politics.headline: Government retreats on working holiday visa cuts after backlash
canberra_politics.body_text: The Albanese government pulled back from cutting working holiday visas, a reversal the Sydney Morning Herald describes as welcome news for regional Australia. The ABC reported the backpacker visa overhaul was softened after backlash, with a Greens senator saying the immigration minister had been 'mugged by reality.'

canberra_politics.headline: NSW Liberals buoyed by internal polling in key battlegrounds
canberra_politics.body_text: The Australian reports internal polling lifting NSW Liberal hopes, with **Kellie Sloane** narrowing the gap on Premier **Chris Minns** in key election battlegrounds. The paper did not publish the underlying figures.

canberra_politics.headline: Victorian leaders' debate heavy on attack, light on policy
canberra_politics.body_text: The ABC's analysis of the Victorian election debate found policy discussion thin but a clear winner in **Jess Wilson**. The Australian framed Labor's **Ben Carroll** as haunted by the Daniel Andrews legacy. Hundreds of pre-poll booths have opened ahead of 1,700 on election day.

canberra_politics.headline: Royal commission hears bikie was paid $165,000 by CFMEU-linked firm
canberra_politics.body_text: Royal Commissioner **Chris Kourakis** warned Bandidos figure **Joel Leavitt** over what the paper called outlandish memory-loss claims, as the inquiry heard he was allegedly paid *$165,000* by a CFMEU-linked firm for no work done. The ABC reported the Victorian royal commission also hearing of building rorts.

business_economy.headline: BloombergNEF warns Australia reaches only 64 percent renewables by 2030
business_economy.body_text: Australia is on track to substantially miss its 2030 renewable energy target, hitting *64 percent* rather than Labor's 82 percent goal, BloombergNEF warned. The projection landed the same day Chris Bowen addressed COP31 in Turkey.

business_economy.headline: Xero declines to confirm New Zealand and Australian job cuts
business_economy.body_text: Xero refused to say whether it is cutting New Zealand and Australian staff after the NZ Herald reported software engineers being told to reapply for a reduced number of roles or take an opt-out package. The company said it 'evolves the structure of its global teams, as needed.' It cut about 800 of 4,500 global roles after Sukhinder Singh Cassidy became chief executive in 2023.

business_economy.headline: Snowy 2.0 cost set to blow out to $75 billion
business_economy.body_text: The Snowy 2.0 pumped hydro scheme is set to blow out to *$75 billion* after what The Australian describes as catastrophic planning failures. The project underpins firming capacity in the national electricity market as coal generators retire.

business_economy.headline: Australian dollar falls to 10-month low as ASX slides
business_economy.body_text: The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low and could fall further, NAB's FX strategist told the ABC. The AUD/USD traded at 0.6734, down 1.59 percent, with the ASX 200 at 8,822, down 3.62 percent, and Brent crude at 89.32, down 6.80 percent.

primary_documents.headline: West Bank settler sanctions
primary_documents.body_text: The Foreign Minister's office published the listing statement for the West Bank settler sanctions, alongside a Parliament House doorstop and interviews with ABC News Breakfast and ABC Radio National on the same measures.

primary_documents.headline: New Zealand's National Statement at COP31
primary_documents.body_text: New Zealand delivered its national statement at COP31, published by the Beehive while the caretaker government travels to APEC in Shenzhen.

calendar_watch.event: US Marine Minerals Administration deep-sea mining lease sale, California
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: A court has blocked the American Samoa component, and the auction would be the first US deep-sea mining lease sale.

calendar_watch.event: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral on the APEC sidelines in Shenzhen
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Albanese and Luxon are both in Shenzhen and have said the outcome on Ukraine is not theirs to shape.
Pre-poll booths are open ahead of 1,700 on election day, with One Nation reported surging in early voting.

calendar_watch.event: Final New Zealand election results declared
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Luxon and McClay are travelling to APEC in caretaker capacity until a government is formed.

key_stat.label: 20-year US compact assistance to three Pacific states
key_stat.context: The broader Compact of Free Association agreements underwriting this year's $450 million tranche also grant Washington exclusive defence rights in Palau, the FSM and the Marshall Islands.

also_today.headline: Elton John warns Albanese against an 'epic self-inflicted error' on AI copyright
also_today.body_text: Elton John urged the Australian government not to let AI companies train on copyrighted work, calling any such move an epic self-inflicted error. The intervention follows this week's campaign by Australian media companies against AI training on their content.

also_today.headline: PNG three-child limit means little without accessible family planning
also_today.body_text: Pacific Beat reports that Papua New Guinea's proposed three-child limit will have little effect while family planning services remain inaccessible across much of the country.

also_today.headline: ASPI: stop reducing artificial intelligence to Big Tech
also_today.body_text: Australia will make better decisions, including for national security, if it treats artificial intelligence as a discovery closer to electricity or the wheel than a product like social media or search, the ASPI Strategist argues.

also_today.headline: Hugh White says Japan and Australia will never be true allies
also_today.body_text: Strategist Hugh White told the ABC's Global Roaming that Japan and Australia will never become true allies, a counterpoint to the Quad's expanded defence announcements in Manila.

also_today.headline: Saab delivers enhanced Royal Australian Navy training capability
also_today.body_text: Saab has provided upgraded training capability to the Royal Australian Navy, Australian Defence Magazine reports. A separate Project of Concern summit was held over the offshore patrol vessel program.

opeds_today.headline: Australia, Philippines Sign New Defense Cooperation Arrangement
opeds_today.central_argument: The arrangement signed in Manila fast-tracks military cooperation between Canberra and Manila.
opeds_today.summary: The Diplomat details the Defence Co-operation Arrangement signed in Manila, which accelerates joint activity between the two militaries.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Adds a second Southeast Asian leg to Australia's maritime security network alongside the Quad commitments announced this week.
